title: The Lighter Brief
overview: Thanksgiving dominated the news this time, mostly in nice ways. Charlotte volunteers served hundreds of free meals, a coonhound named Rocker won the National Dog Show, and the Bears beat the Lions on a last-second throw after a Wu-Tang Clan halftime show. A soggy nor'easter did cause some water hiccups in North Carolina and Maryland, and there's cheerful sports and charity news out of Jamaica too.

stories.headline: Charlotte Rescue Mission serves 500+ Thanksgiving meals
stories.summary: Volunteers at the Charlotte Rescue Mission spent Thanksgiving serving free breakfast and a traditional holiday lunch to anyone who needed one. The team started cooking 60 turkeys two weeks early, and there were movies and table games to make the day feel like family. Staff said the goal was to give everyone a welcoming place for the holiday.
key_facts: More than 500 free meals were served, breakfast and lunch
60 turkeys were cooked, starting two weeks ahead
Kitchen manager Brandy Legree said she was up at 2 a.m. to get ready
The nonprofit also runs addiction recovery programs and welcomes volunteers year-round
stories.why: It's a warm reminder of neighbors looking after neighbors, and the mission is always looking for more helpers.

stories.headline: Wu-Tang rocks Detroit, and the Bears win at the buzzer
stories.summary: Wu-Tang Clan played the Lions' Thanksgiving halftime show at Ford Field, joined by Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer Chad Smith. The nearly seven-minute medley was billed as the wrap-up of their farewell tour. After the long break, the Bears came back to beat the Lions 39-35, and Caleb Williams joked, 'We had 19 minutes to do that. Shoutout to Wu-Tang.'
key_facts: Final score: Bears 39, Lions 35, on a Williams-to-Rome Odunze touchdown with 3 seconds left
Williams threw for 345 yards, and Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 205 yards and 3 TDs for Detroit
Chicago is now 9-2, alone in first place in the NFC North
The show was the second year of the Lions' halftime deal with Eminem and Paul Rosenberg
stories.why: A legendary group's farewell and a thrilling finish made for a memorable holiday game, unless you're a Lions fan.

stories.headline: Marshville, N.C. under a boil water advisory after a main break
stories.summary: A water main broke along Water Plant Road in Marshville on Wednesday afternoon, leaving many residents with little or no water on Thanksgiving. Crews worked overnight, but rain slowed repairs. As service returns, the town has issued a boil water advisory until further notice and apologized for the disrupted holiday.
key_facts: The break happened around 4 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 25
The town first hoped to restore service by 8:30 p.m. that night
The boil water advisory was issued around noon Thursday and stays until the town lifts it
The cause of the break isn't clear yet
stories.why: If you're in Marshville, keep boiling your water until the town says otherwise.

stories.headline: Jamaica's top football league is back on
stories.summary: The Legend Jamaica Premier League will resume this weekend after league operator PFJL and the referees' association settled a dispute over outstanding payments. Referees had stopped working, which halted the competition. PFJL CEO Owen Hill thanked fans for their patience and said new steps will improve accountability and communication.
key_facts: Match Week 12 goes ahead this weekend
The round wraps up with Monday Night Football at the Anthony Spaulding Sports Complex
The dispute was over unpaid officiating fees
stories.why: Fans, players and clubs get their football back, with a plan aimed at avoiding a repeat.

links.title: Legend JPL resumes this weekend after PFJL, referees reach agreement

stories.headline: Jamaica's PM calls for a comeback of cleanliness
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andrew Holness urged Jamaicans to rebuild a culture of cleanliness and better waste habits. He spoke at the Kingston Harbour Clean-up Project site. He said both citizens and government need to do their part, from not littering to regular waste collection.
key_facts: Holness spoke Thursday on Michael Manley Boulevard in Kingston
The event was at the Kingston Harbour Clean-up Project offloading site
stories.why: It's a push toward cleaner public spaces and a healthier harbour.

links.title: Holness urges Jamaicans to rebuild culture of cleanliness

stories.headline: Charlotte dries out with weekend sunshine ahead
stories.summary: After a cold, wet and windy Thanksgiving, the Charlotte area gets sunshine Friday and a pleasant, sunny Saturday. Another round of rain is likely late Sunday, then early next week looks mostly dry. The mountains could get a light dusting of snow.
key_facts: Friday: mostly sunny, breezy, highs in the lower 50s
Saturday: sunny with highs in the 50s
Sunday: highs in the 60s with rain likely late in the afternoon
Mountains could see 1 to 3 inches of snow
stories.why: Saturday looks like the best day for leftover-fueled outdoor plans.

stories.headline: J.Lo saved her Vegas concert film for Thanksgiving
stories.summary: Jennifer Lopez's two-hour concert film 'The JLO Show' premiered Thanksgiving night on CBS and Paramount+. She said she pushed back on a summer release so she could watch it with her family on the holiday. Her mom used to put on West Side Story on Thanksgiving. The film captures the finale of her sold-out Caesars Palace residency.
key_facts: Filmed at the March 28, 2026 finale at the Colosseum at Caesars Palace
Includes her hits plus numbers from West Side Story, Gypsy and Funny Girl
An extended cut is streaming for all Paramount+ subscribers
stories.why: It's a sweet family-tradition story, and a fun watch if you missed it live.

stories.headline: Jamaica's schoolboy football heads into the quarter-finals
stories.summary: The ISSA Urban Under-14 and Under-16 football competitions start their quarter-final group stage on Friday. Eight teams remain in each age group, split into two zones, and the top two in each zone reach the semis. Defending double champions Jamaica College are still alive in both.
key_facts: Kingston College scored 19 goals without conceding in the U-14 second round
KC vs. Jamaica College is a headline U-16 opener
U-14 matches start at 12:30 p.m.
stories.why: It's young talent and old school rivalries on full display.
